newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Russia's GAZ opens Moldovan venture.
newsitem.headline: Russia's GAZ opens Moldovan venture.

text.p: Russia's second biggest carmarker GAZ and Moldova launched a joint venture on Friday to assemble GAZelle minitrucks for small and medium businesses in Moldova and neighbouring states.
"We have decided to focus our attention on the markets within Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union," AO Gorkovsky Avtomobilny Zavod chief executive Nikolai Pugin told a news conference.

Pugin officially opened a joint Moldovan-Russian company which will assemble 2,000 GAZelle minitrucks a year in Chisinau, the capital of Moldova, a former Soviet republic lying between Romania and Ukraine.
GAZelle trucks are already popular among with fledgeling small businesses in the former communist states, whose automobile industries traditionally neglected the small truck sector.
"We understand this venture is a risky deal, because Moldova itself is a tiny market. But production volumes could easily pick up if there is good demand for our truck in other states," he said.
"Small and medium-sized businesses will revive the economies of the Commonwealth of Independent States and Eastern Europe, and our GAZelles will help this," Pugin said.
The first two GAZelles bearing posters in Moldovan "The first Moldovan automobile" and "Safe journey!" left the assembly line as Pugin cut the ribbon to launch the joint venture.
GAZ officials told Reuters they counted on good demand, especially in neighbouring Romania and Bulgaria, for the low consumption trucks trucks with a loading capacity of 1.5 tonnes.
The joint venture is the third in the CIS -- after Almaty in Kazakhstan and Simferopol in Ukraine -- launched by GAZ to break through to new markets.

GAZ chief designer Vladimir Kudryavtsev told Reuters the company would soon soon open new assemblies lines in Kremenchug in Ukraine and Irkutsk in Russia, will raising the annual output of popular trucks by 10,000 to 85,000 from the current 75,000.
He said GAZ would supply its Moldovan partner with nearly 100 percent of necessary components for assembly.

The joint venture called MoldGAZautoservice S.A. i Kompaniya was set up by GAZ together with the Chisinau-based company MoldGAZautoservice which traditionally serves and repairs GAZ cars and trucks in Moldova.
Representatives of both companies declined to name its authorised capital and the shares of each side.
"But we have agreed to divide future profits equally," said MoldGAZautoservice director Victor Miculet.
